title: Lecture 4: Multiprocessor Systems and Modern OS Structures
arabicSummary:
الجزء الأول: أنظمة المعالجات (CPUs) ⚙️

بنشوف إزاي المعالجات (CPUs) بتتوزع جوه الكمبيوتر، وده بيحدد مدى قوة النظام.

1. أنظمة بمعالج واحد (Single Processor System):

كمبيوتر تقليدي فيه CPU واحد بيعمل كل حاجة (شغل الـ OS وشغل المستخدمين). فيه ممكن يكون معالجات متخصصة بتساعده (زي GPU).

2. أنظمة متعددة المعالجات (Multiprocessor Systems / Parallel Systems):

فيها **CPU أو أكتر** بيشاركوا الذاكرة الرئيسية وبيشتغلوا مع بعض. بيسموها كمان **أنظمة متوازية (Parallel)** أو **متصلة بإحكام (Tightly-coupled)**.

ميزاتها:
  • **زيادة الإنتاجية (Increased Throughput):** إنجاز شغل أكتر في نفس الوقت.
  • **اقتصادية (Economy of Scale):** توفير في التكلفة عشان المشاركة في الأجهزة الطرفية وإمدادات الطاقة.
  • **زيادة الموثوقية (Increased Reliability):** لو معالج عطل، النظام بيقدر يشتغل بالباقي (Fault Tolerance).

أنواع أنظمة المعالجات المتعددة:

  • **Symmetric Multiprocessing (SMP):**

    كل المعالجات متساوية وتشتغل معًا، ونواة نظام التشغيل (OS Kernel) بتشتغل على أي معالج فيهم. **(الأكثر استخدامًا)**.

  • **Asymmetric Multiprocessing:**

    كل معالج له وظيفة محددة. معالج واحد هو اللي بيدير النظام (Master) والباقي بيساعده (Slave). (أقل شيوعًا).

الجزء الثاني: أنظمة التشغيل متعددة المهام 💡

1. البرمجة المتعددة (Multiprogramming):

الهدف: المحافظة على الـ CPU مشغول دايمًا. بيتم الاحتفاظ بعدة برامج في الذاكرة الرئيسية (RAM) في نفس الوقت. لما برنامج منهم بيضطر يستنى عملية I/O، الـ OS بيحول التنفيذ لبرنامج تاني، وده بيزود من استخدام الـ CPU.

2. المشاركة الزمنية (Time-Sharing / Multitasking):

الهدف: إعطاء شعور للمستخدم إن الـ CPU بيشتغل عشانه بس. الـ CPU بيقسم وقته على عدة برامج (Jobs) وكل برنامج بياخد شريحة زمنية صغيرة. لما بيخلص وقته، الـ OS بيعمل تبديل سياق (Context Switch) لبرنامج تاني. **النتيجة: استجابة سريعة (Short Response Time) للمستخدم**.

3. الأنظمة الموزعة (Distributed Systems / Loosely Coupled):

مجموعة من أجهزة الكمبيوتر المنفصلة (Nodes) اللي بتشتغل مع بعض على شبكة. كل جهاز له الذاكرة المحلية والـ OS الخاص بيه. أشهر مثال هو **الـ Clusters** اللي بتستخدم في الحوسبة عالية الأداء (HPC).

الجزء الثالث: إدارة الملفات المتقدمة في Linux 📁

أوامر نسخ ونقل وحذف الملفات والمجلدات.

cp source destination: لنسخ ملف (File) أو مجلد (Directory).
cp -r source destination: لنسخ مجلد ومحتوياته بالكامل (Recursively). **ضرورية لنسخ المجلدات!**
mv source destination: لنقل ملف أو مجلد. **(تستخدم أيضًا لتغيير اسم الملف)**.
rm file.txt: لحذف ملف.
rm -r directory_name: لحذف مجلد ومحتوياته بالكامل (خطير جدًا!).
ln -s source_file new_link: لإنشاء رابط رمزي (Symbolic Link) لملف أو مجلد (اختصار).
englishSummary:
Part 1: Processor Systems ⚙️

We look at how processors (CPUs) are distributed within the computer, which determines the system's power.

1. Single Processor System:

A traditional computer with one CPU doing everything (OS tasks and user tasks). It may have specialized processors assisting it (like the GPU).

2. Multiprocessor Systems / Parallel Systems:

Features **multiple CPUs or cores** sharing main memory and working together. They are also called **Parallel Systems** or **Tightly-coupled Systems**.

Advantages:
  • **Increased Throughput:** Accomplishing more work in the same time.
  • **Economy of Scale:** Cost savings due to sharing peripheral devices and power supplies.
  • **Increased Reliability:** If one processor fails, the system can continue operating with the rest (Fault Tolerance).

Types of Multiprocessor Systems:

  • **Symmetric Multiprocessing (SMP):**

    All processors are equal and work together, and the OS Kernel runs on any of them. **(Most common)**.

  • **Asymmetric Multiprocessing:**

    Each processor has a specific function. One processor manages the system (Master) and the others assist it (Slave). (Less common).

Part 2: Multi-Tasking Operating Systems 💡

1. Multiprogramming:

Goal: To keep the CPU busy at all times. Several programs are held in Main Memory (RAM) simultaneously. When one program has to wait for an I/O operation, the OS switches execution to another program, increasing CPU utilization.

2. Time-Sharing / Multitasking:

Goal: To give the user the illusion that the CPU is dedicated to them alone. The CPU divides its time among several programs (Jobs), and each program gets a small time slice. When its time is up, the OS performs a Context Switch to another program. **Result: Short Response Time for the user**.

3. Distributed Systems / Loosely Coupled:

A collection of separate computers (Nodes) working together on a network. Each computer has its local memory and its own OS. The most famous example is **Clusters** used in High-Performance Computing (HPC).

Part 3: Advanced File Management in Linux 📁

Commands for copying, moving, and deleting files and directories.

cp source destination: To copy a file or directory.
cp -r source destination: To copy a directory and its entire contents (Recursively). **Essential for copying directories!**
mv source destination: To move a file or directory. **(Also used to rename a file)**.
rm file.txt: To delete a file.
rm -r directory_name: To delete a directory and its entire contents (Very dangerous!).
ln -s source_file new_link: To create a Symbolic Link to a file or directory (shortcut).

quiz.question: 1. What is the primary goal of Multiprogramming?
options: To allow only one user to use the system
To keep the CPU busy at all times
quiz.correctAnswer: To keep the CPU busy at all times
quiz.hint: عشان الـ CPU ميقعدش فاضي وهو مستني الـ I/O.
quiz.englishHint: To prevent the CPU from being idle while waiting for I/O.

quiz.question: 2. In a Tightly-coupled Multiprocessor system, the CPUs share the:
quiz.englishHint: Shared memory is the basis.

quiz.question: 3. What is the key result of a successful Time-Sharing system?
options: Short response time (< 1 second) for users
quiz.correctAnswer: Short response time (< 1 second) for users
quiz.hint: عشان المستخدم يحس إن النظام سريع.
quiz.englishHint: To make the user feel the system is fast.

quiz.question: 4. The concept of deleting a directory and its contents entirely is called:
quiz.hint: الحذف المتكرر بيحذف كل ما بداخل المجلد.
quiz.englishHint: Recursive deletion deletes everything inside the directory.

quiz.question: 5. Which command is used to copy a directory and its contents recursively in Linux?
quiz.englishHint: 'cp' for copy and 'r' for recursion.

quiz.question: 6. A system where each processor has a specific task (Master/Slave) is called:
quiz.hint: غير متناظر، كل واحد له وظيفة محددة.
quiz.englishHint: Asymmetric, each one has a specific function.

quiz.question: 7. What is the Linux command used to rename a file?
quiz.hint: أمر النقل بيعمل وظيفة تغيير الاسم كمان.
quiz.englishHint: The move command also functions as rename.

quiz.question: 8. What is the term for a system that can continue operating even if one CPU fails?
quiz.englishHint: Reliability and increased possibility.

quiz.question: 9. A system where computers work together over a network, each with its own memory, is called a:
quiz.englishHint: The devices are not tightly coupled.

quiz.question: 10. What does the `ln -s` command create?
quiz.englishHint: The 's' stands for 'symbolic'.

quiz.question: 11. The mechanism used in Time-Sharing to switch between running programs is:
quiz.englishHint: Switching between the context of one program and another.

quiz.question: 12. What is the primary advantage of Symmetric Multiprocessing (SMP)?
options: Only one CPU does all the work
The OS kernel only runs on the Master CPU
All CPUs are equal and can run any part of the OS
It is cheaper than a single processor system
quiz.correctAnswer: All CPUs are equal and can run any part of the OS
quiz.englishHint: Symmetry means equality.

quiz.question: 13. The Linux command to delete a file is:
quiz.englishHint: Short for 'Remove'.

quiz.question: 14. What are Distributed Systems also known as?
quiz.englishHint: Devices are not tightly bound to each other.

quiz.question: 15. What selects which jobs are brought into memory in a Multiprogramming system?
quiz.hint: جزء من الـ Long-Term Scheduler اللي بينظم الشغل.
quiz.englishHint: Part of the Long-Term Scheduler that organizes the work.

quiz.question: 16. Which of these is NOT an advantage of Multiprocessor Systems?
options: Higher power consumption than single systems
quiz.correctAnswer: Higher power consumption than single systems
quiz.englishHint: It is an economic advantage, not a disadvantage.

quiz.question: 17. Which command moves a file from the current directory to the /tmp directory?
quiz.englishHint: The move command.

quiz.question: 18. What is required for a Time-Sharing system to feel interactive?
quiz.englishHint: The response must be very fast.

quiz.question: 19. Sharing peripherals and power supplies is an example of which advantage of multiprocessing?
quiz.englishHint: Cost savings due to sharing.

quiz.question: 20. High-Performance Computing (HPC) often uses clusters for:
options: Running applications in parallel across nodes
quiz.correctAnswer: Running applications in parallel across nodes
quiz.hint: عشان يحلوا مسائل حسابية معقدة بسرعة.
quiz.englishHint: To solve complex computational problems quickly.
